title: Wimbledon Auctions 2023 Blaschka-style shell and wax model false-positive cluster
purpose: Preserve a tightly clustered set of auction lots that are repeatedly retrieved by Blaschka searches but must be excluded from the canonical Blaschka auction table because the auction attribution is explicitly 'in the manner of' and the objects are shell-and-wax anatomical models rather than Blaschka glass models.

cluster_summary.count_guard: Lot 34 is catalogued as two models even though its second numbered description contains (a) and (b) components/species. The title-level model count is retained rather than inventing a separate physical-object ontology from the text alone.
cluster_summary.hammer_total_rule: Arithmetic sum of the five platform-displayed hammer amounts; retained only as sale metadata for the rejected cluster, not as Blaschka market evidence.

rejection_rule.attribution: Every lot is explicitly headed 'IN THE MANNER OF LEOPOLD AND RUDOLF BLASCHKA'.
rejection_rule.material: The lots are described as shell and wax / waxwork anatomical models, not Blaschka glass models.
rejection_rule.literature_use: The catalogue cites UCL and Australian Museum Blaschka literature to contextualise nineteenth-century anatomical modelling and the coexistence of glass, papier-mache and wax models. Citation of Blaschka literature is not maker attribution.

search_contamination_pattern.mechanism: The words 'Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka' appear prominently in the attribution heading and again in cited literature, so maker-name search engines rank these lots highly despite the catalogue itself withholding direct attribution.
search_contamination_pattern.future_rule: When a search result combines Blaschka with wax, shell, papier-mache or 'in the manner of', inspect the lot but do not promote it without independent maker/material evidence.

count_note: The original canonical auction-data.json retained six false-positive records from the first pass. This supplementary cluster adds five researched rejected lots without changing the canonical included-lot count; the combined researched rejected-lot corpus is therefore at least eleven records across the canonical and supplementary layers.
